name: System
author: dbarke
description: CPU and memory on the bar, with per-core load, pressure stalls, temperature and the processes actually responsible in the panel.

barWidget.description: Live CPU and memory readings on the bar; per-core bars, swap, stall pressure, package temperature and the top processes in the panel.

schema.label: Refresh interval (seconds)
schema.description: How often the bar reading is resampled. A CPU percentage is a difference between two samples, so this is also the window it averages over -- longer is calmer, shorter catches short spikes. The panel always samples every second while it is open.

schema.label: Bar reading
schema.description: Which figures sit on the bar. The panel shows everything regardless.

schema.label: Show CPU sparkline
schema.description: A short history strip next to the number, so a spike that already passed is still visible.

schema.label: CPU warning threshold (%)
schema.description: Sustained load at or above this turns the reading urgent. 0 disables.

schema.label: Memory warning threshold (%)
schema.description: Measured against memory that is genuinely unavailable, not against page cache. 0 disables.

schema.label: Show per-core bars
schema.description: One bar per logical CPU. This is what tells a single pegged thread apart from a machine that is actually busy.

schema.label: Processes to list
schema.description: Length of the top-processes table. 0 hides it, and also stops the panel walking /proc for it.

schema.label: Sort processes by
schema.description: Starting sort for the process table. c and m switch it while the panel is open.

schema.label: Full monitor command
schema.description: Launched by b, and by a middle-click on the bar, when the panel is not enough.
